explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly compares LLM evaluation (GPT-4) and human evaluation results, mentioning high consistency between QA-moderation and human evaluation with over 85% agreement ratio.

prompts.notes: Full prompts for helpfulness and harmlessness evaluation shown in figures (Figure 6 and similar for harmlessness); uses multi-response grading with scoring from 1-10

guidelines.notes: Human annotators labeled responses as harmful or harmless based on safety assessment; specific detailed rubric not shown

sample_size.notes: Validation performed on 100 randomly sampled data points from each model

quantitative_scores.notes: Agreement ratio between QA-moderation (LLM evaluation) and human evaluation over 85%

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM evaluation (QA-moderation) and human evaluation show substantial agreement with consistency over 85%, indicating reliability of LLM judgments for safety assessment.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluation assessed both harmlessness and helpfulness using scoring, while human evaluation focused solely on harmfulness (harmful/harmless binary labeling); validation compared harmfulness criterion.
